stated: Expand the Youth Mobility Scheme by: Negotiating with the EU to extend it on a reciprocal basis. Increasing the age limit from 30 to 35. Abolishing the fees for these visas. Extending the length of visas from two to three years.

source.quote: Expand the Youth Mobility Scheme by: Negotiating with the EU to extend it on a reciprocal basis. Increasing the age limit from 30 to 35. Abolishing the fees for these visas. Extending the length of visas from two to three years.

bearing_set.reason: The scheme directly governs young adults' ability to work abroad and vice versa; expanding the age ceiling to 35, extending visa duration to 3 years, abolishing fees, and broadening to EU reciprocity all materially change the employment access and career-development options available to this cohort, earning a real verdict on work and pay.

Easier reciprocal mobility fills genuine skills gaps, improves labour-market matching and productivity, and — crucially — enables UK young people up to 35 to access EU economies for work and skills development, expanding economic opportunity and aggregate living standards on both sides.

A large-scale reciprocal UK–EU youth mobility programme directly increases inter-cultural contact between UK and EU young people living and working in each other's communities, a concrete mechanism for improved social trust and cross-border integration with measurable effects on inter-group contact indicators.

membership_note: Three fundamentals carry a non-negligible verdict: the distributional labour-market effect (O4), the aggregate economic opportunity effect (O13), and the cohesion/inter-group contact effect (O15). Visa fee abolition is real but too narrow (one-off cost to a small applicant population) to earn a meaningful O11 verdict at scale; fiscal revenue loss from fees is too small to move O12 materially.
